round1_to_round2.convergence_assessment: Two different kinds of convergence. (1) The factual inputs converged for good reason: all five now use 125M diluted shares, ~$0.28B net debt today and ~$1.0-1.1B at the horizon, $1.80 CY27 street EPS, $1.81B CY27 revenue and the 23.4-23.7x infrastructure P/E median. These were verified against the 10-Q, the 7/24/26 8-K and Finviz, and agents 1, 3 and 4 say they re-read the filings themselves (agent_3 also read the 13D/A). That is agreement on checked facts, not anchoring. (2) The judgment multiples converged by anchoring on my round-1 file. agent_2's EV/EBITDA leg ($0.95B x 16x less $1.1B = $113) and its $2.40 CY28 EPS are my round-1 numbers verbatim. agent_4's EV/sales of 6.5x on $2.45B is my round-1 leg. agents 2, 4 and 5 all landed on 16x EV/EBITDA, and agents 1, 2, 4 and 5 all landed on a 36-40x PEG-parity P/E, which is my round-1 '~40x' argument. agent_2 says outright that its 14x EV/EBITDA median is 'from the supervisor's recompute ... not re-verified by me'. Only agent_3 (its own MarketScreener 11-peer EV/EBITDA median of 14.2x, no premium, P/E 35x) and agent_1 (its own constant-margin EV/EBITDA basis, 15.6x) built their multiples independently. The tighter fair-value range ($94-108, versus $105-132) is therefore less independent evidence than it looks: count it as about two independent valuation views plus three that follow the supervisor. The ladders moved much less than the fair values (mean P(>=140) 0.464 -> 0.442), because every agent's base scenario ($125-135) still assumes the market keeps a ~55x NTM multiple. Scenario-weighted means of $132-144 sit 30-40% above their own fair values, and none of them reconciles the two.

summary: Round 2 converged on verified facts (125M shares, ~$0.28B net debt, $1.80 CY27 EPS, $1.81B CY27 revenue), and fair values tightened to $94-108. But most of the multiple convergence (16x EV/EBITDA, 36-40x P/E, 6.5x EV/sales) is anchoring on my round-1 file; only agents 1 and 3 rebuilt comps independently.
